title: UN demands inquiry after human rights staffer dies in Houthi detention in Yemen
dek: The UN says a member of its human rights office held by the Houthis since June 2024 died more than a month ago, and his family was told only recently. It is the second UN staff death in Houthi custody, as renewed war in Yemen displaces 290,000 people.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
A staff member of the UN human rights office in Yemen who had been held by the Houthi movement since June 2024 has died in detention, the United Nations said on Saturday, and its human rights chief demanded an independent investigation. The man died more than a month ago, but his family was only recently informed, the UN said, according to Al Jazeera.

UN Secretary-General António Guterres said in a separate statement that he was "appalled" by the death, and the UN said it was urgently seeking answers from the Houthis about what happened. The Houthis, who control the capital Sanaa and much of northern Yemen, had not said how he died.

## What the UN said

The UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, said the man's family "deserve to know the truth" and called for "full transparency" and an "urgent, independent and thorough investigation", Al Jazeera reported. Seven other personnel of his office, the OHCHR, are still being held. "I appeal again for their immediate and unconditional release," Türk said.

The staff member was one of more than 60 people working for the UN and aid groups who were detained in June 2024 and accused by the Houthis of belonging to an "American-Israeli spy network". The UN has rejected such accusations. In all, 72 UN staff and aid workers have been detained by the Houthis, according to Al Jazeera. The Declaration is not naming the man; the UN statement as reported did not give his nationality.

This is the second death of a UN staff member in Houthi custody. A World Food Programme employee died in February 2025, after which the UN paused operations in parts of Houthi-held Yemen. In early October the UN said a WFP employee who had been "arbitrarily detained" had been released.

## A widening war

The death comes as fighting in Yemen intensifies. The UN humanitarian office, OCHA, said at least 290,000 people have been displaced since the war re-erupted in August, particularly in Taiz governorate and along the coast, Al Jazeera reported on Saturday. They include 6,100 pregnant women, 600 of them due to give birth within two weeks. OCHA said 65,000 refugees and asylum seekers in Yemen face a "rapidly deteriorating" situation, and the UN has verified 270 civilian casualties since August, including 68 deaths.

The fighting has spread across the border. The Saudi-led coalition said on Sunday it had intercepted a ballistic missile and a drone fired at southern Saudi Arabia, days after missiles were shot down over Riyadh. Yemen's internationally recognised government says its forces have "neutralised" about 336 Houthi fighters, while the Houthi military spokesman, Yahya Saree, has called Saudi claims about drone attacks "egregious lies". None of these figures could be independently verified.

## Why it matters for India

Yemen sits on the Bab el-Mandeb strait at the southern end of the Red Sea, a route for much of India's trade with Europe. Houthi attacks on shipping from late 2023 forced many vessels to sail around Africa, raising freight costs for Indian exporters. With the Strait of Hormuz already disrupted by the US-Iran conflict, renewed instability around the Red Sea adds to the pressure on India's energy imports and on the many Indian seafarers working on ships in the region.

## What happens next

The UN wants the Houthis to explain the circumstances of the death and release the seven remaining OHCHR detainees. Whether the UN further scales back its aid work in Houthi-held areas, where millions depend on food assistance, will be watched closely.
